newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex to auction projects, vows greater security.
newsitem.headline: Pemex to auction projects, vows greater security.

text.p: Private participation in Mexico's 1997 drilling and refining projects will be set on the auction block later this week, state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) chairman Adrian Lajous said over the weekend.

On Thursday, Pemex will set the bidding for the construction of seven drilling platforms in Campeche Sound, he said, and within a week the bidding for a contract to expand natural gas output in the Burgos Basin in Tamaulipas will be announced.
These and other contracts will auctioned in January, Lajous said while in Mexicali, Baja California at the inauguration of a gasoline storage facility.
A total 10 storage and refining plants were opened in the past months in Salamanca in Guanajuato state, Tula in Hidalgo state and Salina Cruz in Oaxaca state, Lajous said.
"The cost of the 10 plants I just referred to is $410 million," Pemex's chairman said. The company plans to invest an additional 87 percent in 1997, for a total 50.161 billion pesos.
For 1997, Lajous pledged to improve the quality of its products and client service and ensure the safety of its installations, in the face of two fatal accidents in the past six months.
"We have already made the first steps toward designing an integral administration system for the security of our petroleum installations," Lajous said.

A natural gas explosion in July at the Cactus complex cost the company almost $200 million and halted production for months. In November an explosion at a gasoline storage facility outside Mexico City killed four and spawned the ire of locals.
